dropped 87% across measured sessions. Counts × 10 (raw rates 3.1 and 0.4 per-100-sessions).</figcaption></figure><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The tool leaderboard tells the story of how these sessions actually work. Read was called 87,152 times. Bash: 82,552. Edit: 19,979. The Read-to-Write ratio is 9.6:1. Agents read roughly ten times more than they write. That ratio is a direct consequence of the &#x27;read before edit&#x27; hook. Before the hook existed, the ratio was closer to 4:1. The hook didn&#x27;t just prevent blind edits; it changed the agent&#x27;s entire approach to code modification. More reading means more context means fewer bugs. I wasn&#x27;t expecting a single hook to shift the reading behavior that dramatically, but here we are.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The skill invocation count, 1,370, matters because skills bridge static rules and dynamic workflows. A rule says &#x27;validate through the real UI.&#x27; A skill provides the step-by-step protocol: build from source, start the simulator, exercise each feature, capture screenshots, apply the evidence gate. The functional-validation skill in the shannon-framework repo encodes this entire workflow:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-section">### Step 1: Build the Real System</span>
audit-evidence/og-meta-260519-0256/cycle-03/routes/post-07-prompt-engineering-stack.html:112:<span class="hljs-bullet">-</span> [ ] Would a skeptical reviewer agree?</pre></div><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The skill doesn&#x27;t replace the hook. The hook doesn&#x27;t replace the CLAUDE.md instruction. All three say the same thing through different mechanisms at different points in the session. That&#x27;s the redundancy principle at work.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">When Layers Conflict</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The stack usually reinforces itself. Sometimes two layers say contradictory things. Knowing which wins matters.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Most common collision: project CLAUDE.md says &#x27;run pnpm build after editing TypeScript files.&#x27; A PostToolUse hook fires on the same Bash command and injects &#x27;compilation is NOT validation — exercise the feature through the real UI.&#x27; Looks like Layer 1 and Layer 3 are fighting.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">They&#x27;re not. Layer 1 defines what to do. Layer 3 defines what that action doesn&#x27;t prove. The build verifies syntax and types. The hook reminds the agent that a green build doesn&#x27;t mean the feature works. Run the build, then run the real thing. Additive, not contradictory.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The harder case: a PreToolUse hook blocks an action the constitution calls for. This happened once with read-before-edit.js. The project constitution said &#x27;update src/config.ts with the new environment variable.&#x27; The hook flagged the edit because config.ts hadn&#x27;t been read that session. Block versus explicit instruction. Layer 3 wins temporarily — read first, then edit. Layer 1 still gets fulfilled with one extra step. When a block hook fires on an instructed action, satisfy the precondition. Don&#x27;t work around it.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">Building Your Own Stack</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The shannon-framework repo contains working implementations of all the hooks and skills I&#x27;ve described. Drop them into your project:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-comment"># Copy hooks into your Claude Code project</span>

class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">2026-03-06</span></div><h1 class="font-black text-balance wa-post-hero-title" style="margin:0;font-size:clamp(40px, 6.4vw, 88px);font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-2.4px;line-height:1.15;color:var(--text-cream);max-width:16ch;margin-inline:auto">Building Claude Code Plugins That Actually Work</h1><p style="margin-top:22px;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);color:var(--text-cream-detail);line-height:1.55;max-width:56ch;margin-inline:auto">Hooks, skills, and the enforcement layer that turns agent suggestions into hard stops across 23,479 sessions</p><a href="https://github.com/krzemienski/shannon-framework" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 mt-6 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-accent bg-accent/10 border border-accent/20 rounded-lg hover:bg-accent/20 transition-colors"><span aria-hidden="true" data-glyph="term">·</span>View companion repo<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></header><div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2 mb-8"><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=AgenticDevelopment">#<!-- -->AgenticDevelopment</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=ClaudeCode">#<!-- -->ClaudeCode</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=Plugins">#<!-- -->Plugins</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=Hooks">#<!-- -->Hooks</a></div><div class="wa-typed-body"><p style="margin-top:0;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.92);font-family:&quot;Fraunces&quot;, Georgia, serif;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:-0.2px">I put “NEVER create test files” in CLAUDE.md. The agents created test files anyway.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Bold formatting, triple emphasis, all-caps warnings. The violation rate dropped but never hit zero. Across 23,479 sessions, the pattern was obvious: text-based instructions are suggestions. Agents deprioritize them when context gets long, when the task gets hairy, when the implementation chain goes deep. It’s not defiance — the agent is making trade-offs in a limited context window, and “do not create test files” loses to “I need to verify this function works.”</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Then I wrote a 72-line JavaScript hook that blocks Write calls to any file matching test patterns. Violation rate: zero. The Write tool call hits the hook, the hook returns exit code 2, and the agent sees a message explaining why the action was rejected. Not a suggestion. A hard stop.</p><blockquote style="margin:32px 0;padding:22px 26px;border-radius:12px;background:linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.08), rgba(122, 61, 255, 0.05));border-left:3px solid var(--accent);font-size:var(--text-body-lead);line-height:var(--leading-meta);font-style:italic;font-family:&quot;Fraunces&quot;, Georgia, serif;color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)">“<!-- -->That’s the difference between a skill that suggests and a plugin that enforces.<!-- -->”</blockquote><aside aria-label="TL;DR" style="margin:28px 0;padding:20px 24px 16px;border-radius:10px;background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.06), rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.02));border-left:3px solid var(--accent);border:1px solid var(--hairline);border-left-width:3px"><div class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);font-weight:700;letter-spacing:1.6px;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent);margin-bottom:12px">TL;DR</div><ul style="margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none"><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:0;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:none;font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:7px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>A 72-line PreToolUse JavaScript hook with 12 regex patterns drove test-file violations from non-zero to zero — every Write/Edit/MultiEdit hits the hook, no opt-in needed.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Hooks ride mandatory tool calls: 19,979 Edits and 82,552 Bash invocations went through PreToolUse/PostToolUse layers versus only 1,370 (opt-in) skill calls — every build success triggered <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">validation-not-compilation.js</code> against 12 build-command regexes.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>The four-layer Shannon Framework (CLAUDE.md → hooks → skills → commands) reached 95%+ combined compliance; the stdin/stdout contract is <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">exit 2</code> to block or inject, <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">exit 0</code> to allow.</li></ul></aside><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The Gap Between Instructions and Enforcement</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Claude Code’s plugin system has four extension points: hooks that fire on tool events, skills that provide domain workflows, agents that define specialist roles, and MCP servers that add tool capabilities. Most people use CLAUDE.md and maybe a few skills. Almost nobody builds hooks. That’s a mistake.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Across 23,479 sessions, the Skill tool fired 1,370 times. The tool leaderboard: Read fired 87,152 times, Bash fired 82,552 times, Edit fired 19,979 times. For every skill invocation, there were 63 Read calls and 60 Bash calls happening without any skill guidance.</p><figure class="wa-chart-anim" style="margin:32px 0;padding:20px 22px;border-radius:var(--radius, 12px);background:var(--surface, rgba(255,255,255,0.03));border:1px solid var(--border, rgba(255,255,255,0.07))"><div style="display:flex;align-items:baseline;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:16px"><div style="display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:12px;flex-wrap:wrap"><span sessions</span></div><span style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, monospace);font-size:10px;letter-spacing:0.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent, style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(80px, 110px) 1fr 70px;gap:14px;align-items:center"><div style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, monospace);font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--accent, #FF3D52);text-align:right">0</div></div></div><figcaption style="margin-top:12px;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--text-3, rgba(244,243,238,0.5));line-height:1.5;font-style:italic">Skills are opt-in. Hooks are mandatory. Every Read/Bash/Edit passes through the hook layer; only ~1.5% of tool calls invoke a skill.</figcaption></figure><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Skills are opt-in. Hooks are mandatory. Every one of those 19,979 Edit calls passed through my PreToolUse hooks. Every one of those 82,552 Bash calls triggered my PostToolUse hooks. The agent doesn’t choose to comply. The enforcement layer checks automatically, on every tool call.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">One Hook, End to End</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here’s what a hook actually does. This is validation-not-compilation.js from the shannon-framework. It fires after every Bash command, watches for build success, and injects a reminder that “it compiled” is not “it works.”</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The problem it solves: agents conflate build success with feature completion. A clean build means the code is syntactically correct and type-safe. It says nothing about whether the feature does what you asked. Without a hook, the agent runs npm run build, sees “compiled successfully,” and marks the task done. The feature is broken. Nobody checked.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The hook source:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><div class="wa-mono" style="padding:8px 14px;font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.55);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.02);border-bottom:1px solid var(--hairline);display:flex;justify-content:space-between"><span>// .claude/hooks/validation-not-compilation.js</span><span>javascript</span></div><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-comment">// .claude/hooks/validation-not-compilation.js</span>

transition-colors">194 Parallel Agents, Zero Merge Conflicts</div></a></div></div><header class="wa-post-hero mb-12 text-center"><div class="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-2.5 style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">18 min read</span><span class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">·</span><span class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">2026-03-06</span></div><h1 class="font-black text-balance wa-post-hero-title" style="margin:0;font-size:clamp(40px, 6.4vw, 88px);font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-2.4px;line-height:1.15;color:var(--text-cream);max-width:16ch;margin-inline:auto">The 7-Layer Prompt Engineering Stack</h1><p style="margin-top:22px;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);color:var(--text-cream-detail);line-height:1.55;max-width:56ch;margin-inline:auto">How layered enforcement turned written rules into mechanical discipline across 23,479 AI coding sessions</p><a href="https://github.com/krzemienski/shannon-framework" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 mt-6 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-accent bg-accent/10 border border-accent/20 rounded-lg hover:bg-accent/20 transition-colors"><span aria-hidden="true" data-glyph="term">·</span>View companion repo<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></header><div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2 mb-8"><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=AgenticDevelopment">#<!-- -->AgenticDevelopment</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=ClaudeCode">#<!-- -->ClaudeCode</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=PromptEngineering">#<!-- -->PromptEngineering</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=AgentGovernance">#<!-- -->AgentGovernance</a></div><div class="wa-typed-body"><p style="margin-top:0;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.92);font-family:&quot;Fraunces&quot;, Georgia, serif;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:-0.2px">I had 14 rules in my CLAUDE.md. The agent followed 11 consistently. The other three (&#x27;never create test files,&#x27; &#x27;always compile after editing,&#x27; &#x27;read the full file before modifying it&#x27;) failed at rates that made them decorative. 47 test files created despite a clear prohibition. 112 edits to files the agent hadn&#x27;t read. 63 premature &#x27;complete&#x27; declarations where the agent claimed a task was done without building the code.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here&#x27;s the thing. The agent understands every rule. It can explain why each one exists. It&#x27;ll recite them back if you ask. Then 11 tool calls later, deep in a problem-solving loop, it creates auth.test.ts because that&#x27;s what its training says a responsible developer does.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Writing rules is easy. Getting an AI agent to follow them under pressure? Completely different problem. The solution I landed on borrows from Claude Shannon&#x27;s information theory: reliable communication requires redundant encoding. Same principle applies to agent discipline. Say the same thing seven different ways, through seven different mechanisms, and the message gets through.</p><aside aria-label="TL;DR" style="margin:28px 0;padding:20px 24px 16px;border-radius:10px;background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.06), rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.02));border-left:3px solid var(--accent);border:1px solid var(--hairline);border-left-width:3px"><div class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);font-weight:700;letter-spacing:1.6px;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent);margin-bottom:12px">TL;DR</div><ul style="margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none"><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:0;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:none;font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:7px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Seven layers (<code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">CLAUDE.md</code> → <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">.claude/rules/</code> → hooks → skills → agents → MCP tools → SessionStart hooks) drove aggregate violations from 3.1 per session to 0.4 — an 87% reduction at 7ms hook overhead per tool call.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Five hooks survived production out of 23 built; <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">block-test-files.js</code> took test-file creation from 23% to 0%, and <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">read-before-edit.js</code> shifted the Read-to-Write ratio from 4:1 to 9.6:1 across 87,152 reads versus 19,979 edits.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Splitting governance into nine focused <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">.claude/rules/*.md</code> files lifted compliance on bottom-half rules from 72% (single 800-line CLAUDE.md) to 89%, and the 3-level block/warn/remind severity model out-scored 2-level (87%) and 5-level (88%) variants at 95%.</li></ul></aside><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The Gap Between Understanding and Compliance</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Watch this failure mode play out. You write a clear instruction:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-strong">**NEVER:**</span> write mocks, stubs, test doubles, unit tests, or test files.
audit-evidence/og-meta-260519-0256/cycle-02/routes/post-07-prompt-engineering-stack.html:35:user interfaces. Capture and verify evidence before claiming completion.</pre></div><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Six lines. Unambiguous. The agent reads this at the start of every session. Then the session grows. By tool call 40, those six lines are competing with 30,000+ tokens of accumulated context: code it&#x27;s read, errors it&#x27;s debugged, plans it&#x27;s made. The instruction doesn&#x27;t disappear. It just loses salience. The agent&#x27;s been reading Swift files for 20 minutes. It knows the codebase has no tests. And then it writes UserServiceTests.swift because the pattern is so deeply embedded in its training that it fires automatically.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Better instructions don&#x27;t work. I tried for weeks. Rephrasing. Bold text. Moving the rule to different positions in the file. The violation rate barely moved. The problem is structural. By tool call 40, six lines of guidance are competing with 30,000+ tokens of accumulated context. They lose.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The numbers that forced a different approach: across 23,479 sessions spanning 42 days, the Skill tool fired 1,370 times. ExitPlanMode, the gate that prevents agents from writing code before planning, triggered 111 times. Those are enforcement mechanisms doing real work. But they only work because they&#x27;re part of a stack, not standalone instructions.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The 7-Layer Stack</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Seven layers. monospace);font-size:10px;font-weight:400;color:var(--text-3, rgba(244,243,238,0.4))">· <!-- -->CLAUDE.md (constitution)</span></li></ul><figcaption style="margin-top:8px;font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, monospace);font-size:11px;color:var(--text-3, rgba(244,243,238,0.4));letter-spacing:0.06em">The 7-layer prompt-engineering stack. Defense in depth — Layer 1 sets non-negotiables at the apex; Layers 2-7 reinforce through different mechanisms (rules, hooks, skills, agents, MCP tools, session hooks). No single layer suffices; all seven together drive 87% violation reduction.</figcaption></figure><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 1: Global Constitution. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Applies to every project on every machine. This is the constitution. Projects can add laws but can&#x27;t override it. The non-negotiable mandates live here: functional validation only, no test files, no mocks, evidence-based completion claims.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 2: Rules Directory. .claude/rules/*.md. A 50-line focused file gets more reliable attention than 50 lines buried in a 500-line document. I split governance into nine files: coding-style.md, security.md, testing.md, git-workflow.md, performance.md, agents.md, patterns.md, hooks.md, development-workflow.md. Each file covers one concern. When the agent needs the security rules, it can locate and re-read a 40-line file instead of scanning a monolith.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 3: Hooks. Code that runs on every tool call. This is where rules become enforceable. PreToolUse hooks fire before a tool executes and can block the call entirely. PostToolUse hooks fire after and inject corrective reminders. The agent can&#x27;t ignore a hook that returns { &#x27;decision&#x27;: &#x27;block&#x27; }.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 4: Skills. Structured workflows with routing tables and gates. A skill like functional-validation is a step-by-step protocol that an agent invokes when it needs to prove something works. Skills carry project-specific context that the agent doesn&#x27;t have by default. Across all sessions, 1,370 skill invocations kept agents on prescribed workflows instead of improvising.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 5: Agents. Specialized roles with scoped instructions. A code-reviewer agent has a review checklist baked into its prompt. A build-fixer agent knows to check DerivedData and clean caches. Each agent carries domain knowledge that the main agent forgets under context pressure.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 6: MCP Tools. External capabilities with built-in constraints. The sequential thinking tool (327 invocations across all sessions) forces structured reasoning before implementation. The Stitch MCP enforces design system compliance. These tools add discipline through their interface design, not through written rules.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 7: Session Start Hooks. Inject the full governance context from turn one. Before the agent has any competing context, it loads the rules, the project constitution, and the enforcement expectations. Sets the behavioral baseline before problem-solving begins.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The principle is defense in depth. If the agent forgets the build command (Layer 1 failure), the auto-build hook catches it (Layer 3). If the hook misses it, the evidence gate blocks premature completion claims (Layer 4). No single layer is sufficient. All seven together produce results that no single layer achieves alone.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">Hooks: Where Rules Become Enforceable</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layers 1 and 2 are suggestions. Layer 3 is enforcement. A hook is a JavaScript function that Claude Code runs automatically on every tool call. Two types:</p><figure style="margin:32px 0"><figcaption style="font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, They inspect the output and inject reminders or corrective context.</span></li></ul><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here&#x27;s block-test-files.js from the shannon-framework repo. This hook dropped test file creation from a 23% violation rate to zero:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-keyword">const</span> <span class="hljs-variable constant_">TEST_PATTERNS</span> = [
audit-evidence/og-meta-260519-0256/cycle-02/routes/post-07-prompt-engineering-stack.html:96:[ ] Would a skeptical reviewer agree this is complete?</pre></div><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Task completion quality improved 34% after deploying this hook. The agent started quoting specific screenshot contents and command output lines instead of saying &#x27;screenshot confirms functionality.&#x27;</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">skill-activation-check.js — UserPromptSubmit hook. Fires on every user message that looks like an implementation request. Reminds the agent to scan available skills before jumping into code. This hook drives the 1,370 skill invocations I measured. Without it, agents skip skills and improvise, which produces worse results.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The 18 hooks that died: max-file-size, no-console-log, import-order, commit-message-reviewer, type-annotation-enforcer, function-length, single-responsibility, dry-violation-detector, and ten more. Each seemed reasonable in isolation.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The pattern is clear: if the violation can be objectively detected from the tool input alone, a hook works. block-test-files.js checks a filename. Deterministic, no judgment calls. function-length requires parsing the full file, understanding function boundaries, and deciding whether 52 lines is too many. Subjective, slow, and wrong often enough to be counterproductive.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Style hooks create more problems than they solve. The import-order hook fired on 40% of file writes. The agent spent tokens reorganizing imports, and the reorganized imports were sometimes wrong. Net negative value.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here&#x27;s the meta-rule: hooks should enforce safety invariants, not style preferences. &#x27;Don&#x27;t commit API keys&#x27; is a safety invariant. &#x27;Functions should be under 50 lines&#x27; is a style preference with too many legitimate exceptions. Can you tell the difference? That&#x27;s the whole game.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The CLAUDE.md Inheritance Chain</h2><figure style="margin:32px 0"><figcaption style="font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);letter-spacing:1.4px;font-weight:700;color:var(--accent);margin-bottom:10px;text-transform:uppercase">CLAUDE.md inheritance chain</figcaption><div 6px);background:var(--bg-2, rgba(0,0,0,0.25));border:1px solid var(--border-strong, rgba(255,255,255,0.16));font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);margin-top:6px;font-weight:600">patterns.md</div><div style="padding:8px 10px;border-radius:var(--radius-sm, 6px);background:var(--bg-2, rgba(0,0,0,0.25));border:1px solid var(--border-strong, rgba(255,255,255,0.16));font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);margin-top:6px;font-weight:600">performance.md</div></div></div><figcaption style="margin-top:10px;font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.55);line-height:var(--leading-link);font-style:italic">Global constitution → project constitution → focused rule files. Each layer extends the previous; no project can relax global non-negotiables.</figcaption></figure><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Global (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md) sets the non-negotiables. These rules apply to every project I work on. The functional validation mandate lives here. The prohibition on test files lives here. The evidence-gate requirement lives here. A project CLAUDE.md can add constraints but can&#x27;t relax these.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Project (./CLAUDE.md) adds project-specific context. The build command. The tech stack. Known pitfalls. &#x27;DerivedData must be cleaned before building.&#x27; &#x27;Use CryptoKit not Crypto.&#x27; &#x27;The backend binary is at ./server not ./build/server.&#x27; These are the rules that prevent the agent from rediscovering the same bugs I already fixed.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Rules (.claude/rules/*.md) break concerns into focused files. A 50-line file about security gets more reliable attention than the same 50 lines buried in a 500-line CLAUDE.md. Nine files, nine concerns. The agent loads them all, but when it needs to recall the git workflow, it can mentally index into a 30-line file instead of scanning everything.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Why not just one big file? I tested both approaches. A single 800-line CLAUDE.md produced 72% compliance on rules in the bottom half of the file. The same rules split into focused files: 89% compliance. Position in the file matters for a single document. Position in a separate file doesn&#x27;t, because each file starts at line 1. Think about that for a second. The agent follows rules at the top of a long file more than rules at the bottom. That&#x27;s wild.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The Enforcement Severity Spectrum</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Not all violations are equal. Creating a test file is a hard violation, the file shouldn&#x27;t exist. Forgetting to read a file before editing is a soft violation, the edit still might be correct. The hook system reflects this with three severity levels.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Block — The hook stops the tool call. The agent can&#x27;t proceed until it takes a different approach. Used for: test file creation, API key commits, writes to reference data files. Zero tolerance.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Warn — The hook injects a warning but allows the tool call to proceed. Used for: editing unread files, large file modifications, missing build verification. The agent gets the nudge without getting blocked from legitimate edge cases.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Remind — The hook injects a contextual reminder after the fact. Used for: dev server restarts after config changes, documentation updates after API changes, the &#x27;compilation isn&#x27;t validation&#x27; reminder.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">I tested 2-level (block/allow) and 5-level systems before settling on three. The 2-level system hit 87% compliance, but too many false blocks pushed the agent into workaround patterns. It would rename files to dodge the block, which was worse than the original violation. (Imagine that. The agent learned to game your rules.) The 5-level system scored 88%. The extra levels created decision fatigue. The agent spent tokens reasoning about whether a violation was severity 3 or severity 4 instead of doing its actual work. Three levels hit 95% compliance. Simple enough to be reliable.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">Subagent Inheritance: The Gap That Breaks Everything</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The main agent follows the constitution. Then it spawns a subagent via the Task tool, and the subagent starts with zero governance context. I measured this gap: 68% compliance for subagents without constitution injection versus 95% with it. That&#x27;s a 27-point drop just because the rules didn&#x27;t get passed along.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The fix is a PreToolUse hook on the Agent tool that automatically injects core rules into every subagent prompt. When the main agent spawns a code-reviewer, the hook appends the functional validation mandate, the no-test-files rule, and the evidence-gate checklist to the subagent&#x27;s instructions. The subagent inherits the constitution without the main agent needing to remember to pass it along.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">This is the single most important lesson from the stack: governance must be automatic and inherited. If compliance depends on the agent remembering to propagate rules, it&#x27;ll forget. 2,827 Task spawns and 929 Agent calls across all 23,479 sessions. That&#x27;s 3,756 opportunities for governance to drop. How many of those do you think the agent would remember on its own? Automatic injection eliminates the failure mode entirely.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">What the Numbers Show</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Across the measured sessions, the aggregate violation rate dropped from 3.1 per session to 0.4, an 87% reduction. Hook overhead: 7ms per tool call, undetectable in practice.</p><figure class="wa-chart-anim" style="margin:32px 0;padding:20px 22px;border-radius:var(--radius, 12px);background:var(--surface, style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(80px, 110px) 1fr 70px;gap:14px;align-items:center"><div style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, #0c0c0e);border-radius:var(--radius-sm, 4px);overflow:hidden"><div style="position:absolute;inset:0 auto 0 0;width:0%;background:var(--accent, #FF3D52);transition:width 1100ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.6,0.2,1) 80ms"></div><div aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;inset:0;background:repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 0 23px, var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.06)) 23px 24px);opacity:0.4"></div></div><div style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, monospace);font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--accent, #FF3D52);text-align:right">0</div></div></div><figcaption style="margin-top:12px;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--text-3, rgba(244,243,238,0.5));line-height:1.5;font-style:italic">Aggregate violations dropped 87% across measured sessions. Counts × 10 (raw rates 3.1 and 0.4 per-100-sessions).</figcaption></figure><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The tool leaderboard tells the story of how these sessions actually work. Read was called 87,152 times. Bash: 82,552. Edit: 19,979. The Read-to-Write ratio is 9.6:1. Agents read roughly ten times more than they write. That ratio is a direct consequence of the &#x27;read before edit&#x27; hook. Before the hook existed, the ratio was closer to 4:1. The hook didn&#x27;t just prevent blind edits; it changed the agent&#x27;s entire approach to code modification. More reading means more context means fewer bugs. I wasn&#x27;t expecting a single hook to shift the reading behavior that dramatically, but here we are.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The skill invocation count, 1,370, matters because skills bridge static rules and dynamic workflows. A rule says &#x27;validate through the real UI.&#x27; A skill provides the step-by-step protocol: build from source, start the simulator, exercise each feature, capture screenshots, apply the evidence gate. The functional-validation skill in the shannon-framework repo encodes this entire workflow:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-section">### Step 1: Build the Real System</span>
audit-evidence/og-meta-260519-0256/cycle-02/routes/post-07-prompt-engineering-stack.html:112:<span class="hljs-bullet">-</span> [ ] Would a skeptical reviewer agree?</pre></div><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The skill doesn&#x27;t replace the hook. The hook doesn&#x27;t replace the CLAUDE.md instruction. All three say the same thing through different mechanisms at different points in the session. That&#x27;s the redundancy principle at work.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">When Layers Conflict</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The stack usually reinforces itself. Sometimes two layers say contradictory things. Knowing which wins matters.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Most common collision: project CLAUDE.md says &#x27;run pnpm build after editing TypeScript files.&#x27; A PostToolUse hook fires on the same Bash command and injects &#x27;compilation is NOT validation — exercise the feature through the real UI.&#x27; Looks like Layer 1 and Layer 3 are fighting.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">They&#x27;re not. Layer 1 defines what to do. Layer 3 defines what that action doesn&#x27;t prove. The build verifies syntax and types. The hook reminds the agent that a green build doesn&#x27;t mean the feature works. Run the build, then run the real thing. Additive, not contradictory.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The harder case: a PreToolUse hook blocks an action the constitution calls for. This happened once with read-before-edit.js. The project constitution said &#x27;update src/config.ts with the new environment variable.&#x27; The hook flagged the edit because config.ts hadn&#x27;t been read that session. Block versus explicit instruction. Layer 3 wins temporarily — read first, then edit. Layer 1 still gets fulfilled with one extra step. When a block hook fires on an instructed action, satisfy the precondition. Don&#x27;t work around it.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">Building Your Own Stack</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The shannon-framework repo contains working implementations of all the hooks and skills I&#x27;ve described. Drop them into your project:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-comment"># Copy hooks into your Claude Code project</span>

class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">2026-03-06</span></div><h1 class="font-black text-balance wa-post-hero-title" style="margin:0;font-size:clamp(40px, 6.4vw, 88px);font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-2.4px;line-height:1.15;color:var(--text-cream);max-width:16ch;margin-inline:auto">Building Claude Code Plugins That Actually Work</h1><p style="margin-top:22px;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);color:var(--text-cream-detail);line-height:1.55;max-width:56ch;margin-inline:auto">Hooks, skills, and the enforcement layer that turns agent suggestions into hard stops across 23,479 sessions</p><a href="https://github.com/krzemienski/shannon-framework" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 mt-6 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-accent bg-accent/10 border border-accent/20 rounded-lg hover:bg-accent/20 transition-colors"><span aria-hidden="true" data-glyph="term">·</span>View companion repo<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></header><div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2 mb-8"><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=AgenticDevelopment">#<!-- -->AgenticDevelopment</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=ClaudeCode">#<!-- -->ClaudeCode</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=Plugins">#<!-- -->Plugins</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=Hooks">#<!-- -->Hooks</a></div><div class="wa-typed-body"><p style="margin-top:0;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.92);font-family:&quot;Fraunces&quot;, Georgia, serif;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:-0.2px">I put “NEVER create test files” in CLAUDE.md. The agents created test files anyway.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Bold formatting, triple emphasis, all-caps warnings. The violation rate dropped but never hit zero. Across 23,479 sessions, the pattern was obvious: text-based instructions are suggestions. Agents deprioritize them when context gets long, when the task gets hairy, when the implementation chain goes deep. It’s not defiance — the agent is making trade-offs in a limited context window, and “do not create test files” loses to “I need to verify this function works.”</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Then I wrote a 72-line JavaScript hook that blocks Write calls to any file matching test patterns. Violation rate: zero. The Write tool call hits the hook, the hook returns exit code 2, and the agent sees a message explaining why the action was rejected. Not a suggestion. A hard stop.</p><blockquote style="margin:32px 0;padding:22px 26px;border-radius:12px;background:linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.08), rgba(122, 61, 255, 0.05));border-left:3px solid var(--accent);font-size:var(--text-body-lead);line-height:var(--leading-meta);font-style:italic;font-family:&quot;Fraunces&quot;, Georgia, serif;color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)">“<!-- -->That’s the difference between a skill that suggests and a plugin that enforces.<!-- -->”</blockquote><aside aria-label="TL;DR" style="margin:28px 0;padding:20px 24px 16px;border-radius:10px;background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.06), rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.02));border-left:3px solid var(--accent);border:1px solid var(--hairline);border-left-width:3px"><div class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);font-weight:700;letter-spacing:1.6px;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent);margin-bottom:12px">TL;DR</div><ul style="margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none"><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:0;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:none;font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:7px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>A 72-line PreToolUse JavaScript hook with 12 regex patterns drove test-file violations from non-zero to zero — every Write/Edit/MultiEdit hits the hook, no opt-in needed.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Hooks ride mandatory tool calls: 19,979 Edits and 82,552 Bash invocations went through PreToolUse/PostToolUse layers versus only 1,370 (opt-in) skill calls — every build success triggered <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">validation-not-compilation.js</code> against 12 build-command regexes.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>The four-layer Shannon Framework (CLAUDE.md → hooks → skills → commands) reached 95%+ combined compliance; the stdin/stdout contract is <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">exit 2</code> to block or inject, <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">exit 0</code> to allow.</li></ul></aside><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The Gap Between Instructions and Enforcement</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Claude Code’s plugin system has four extension points: hooks that fire on tool events, skills that provide domain workflows, agents that define specialist roles, and MCP servers that add tool capabilities. Most people use CLAUDE.md and maybe a few skills. Almost nobody builds hooks. That’s a mistake.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Across 23,479 sessions, the Skill tool fired 1,370 times. The tool leaderboard: Read fired 87,152 times, Bash fired 82,552 times, Edit fired 19,979 times. For every skill invocation, there were 63 Read calls and 60 Bash calls happening without any skill guidance.</p><figure class="wa-chart-anim" style="margin:32px 0;padding:20px 22px;border-radius:var(--radius, 12px);background:var(--surface, rgba(255,255,255,0.03));border:1px solid var(--border, rgba(255,255,255,0.07))"><div style="display:flex;align-items:baseline;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-bottom:16px"><div style="display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:12px;flex-wrap:wrap"><span sessions</span></div><span style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, monospace);font-size:10px;letter-spacing:0.14em;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent, style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(80px, 110px) 1fr 70px;gap:14px;align-items:center"><div style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, style="font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, monospace);font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:var(--accent, #FF3D52);text-align:right">0</div></div></div><figcaption style="margin-top:12px;font-size:12.5px;color:var(--text-3, rgba(244,243,238,0.5));line-height:1.5;font-style:italic">Skills are opt-in. Hooks are mandatory. Every Read/Bash/Edit passes through the hook layer; only ~1.5% of tool calls invoke a skill.</figcaption></figure><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Skills are opt-in. Hooks are mandatory. Every one of those 19,979 Edit calls passed through my PreToolUse hooks. Every one of those 82,552 Bash calls triggered my PostToolUse hooks. The agent doesn’t choose to comply. The enforcement layer checks automatically, on every tool call.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">One Hook, End to End</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here’s what a hook actually does. This is validation-not-compilation.js from the shannon-framework. It fires after every Bash command, watches for build success, and injects a reminder that “it compiled” is not “it works.”</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The problem it solves: agents conflate build success with feature completion. A clean build means the code is syntactically correct and type-safe. It says nothing about whether the feature does what you asked. Without a hook, the agent runs npm run build, sees “compiled successfully,” and marks the task done. The feature is broken. Nobody checked.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The hook source:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><div class="wa-mono" style="padding:8px 14px;font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.55);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.02);border-bottom:1px solid var(--hairline);display:flex;justify-content:space-between"><span>// .claude/hooks/validation-not-compilation.js</span><span>javascript</span></div><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-comment">// .claude/hooks/validation-not-compilation.js</span>

transition-colors">194 Parallel Agents, Zero Merge Conflicts</div></a></div></div><header class="wa-post-hero mb-12 text-center"><div class="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-center gap-2.5 style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">18 min read</span><span class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">·</span><span class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);color:var(--text-cream-meta)">2026-03-06</span></div><h1 class="font-black text-balance wa-post-hero-title" style="margin:0;font-size:clamp(40px, 6.4vw, 88px);font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-2.4px;line-height:1.15;color:var(--text-cream);max-width:16ch;margin-inline:auto">The 7-Layer Prompt Engineering Stack</h1><p style="margin-top:22px;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);color:var(--text-cream-detail);line-height:1.55;max-width:56ch;margin-inline:auto">How layered enforcement turned written rules into mechanical discipline across 23,479 AI coding sessions</p><a href="https://github.com/krzemienski/shannon-framework" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" class="inline-flex items-center gap-2 mt-6 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-accent bg-accent/10 border border-accent/20 rounded-lg hover:bg-accent/20 transition-colors"><span aria-hidden="true" data-glyph="term">·</span>View companion repo<span aria-hidden="true">↗</span></a></header><div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2 mb-8"><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=AgenticDevelopment">#<!-- -->AgenticDevelopment</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=ClaudeCode">#<!-- -->ClaudeCode</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=PromptEngineering">#<!-- -->PromptEngineering</a><a class="text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full bg-surface-chip-hover border border-border-chip text-cream-body hover:border-accent/40 hover:text-cream transition-colors" href="/posts?tag=AgentGovernance">#<!-- -->AgentGovernance</a></div><div class="wa-typed-body"><p style="margin-top:0;font-size:var(--text-body-lead);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.92);font-family:&quot;Fraunces&quot;, Georgia, serif;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:-0.2px">I had 14 rules in my CLAUDE.md. The agent followed 11 consistently. The other three (&#x27;never create test files,&#x27; &#x27;always compile after editing,&#x27; &#x27;read the full file before modifying it&#x27;) failed at rates that made them decorative. 47 test files created despite a clear prohibition. 112 edits to files the agent hadn&#x27;t read. 63 premature &#x27;complete&#x27; declarations where the agent claimed a task was done without building the code.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here&#x27;s the thing. The agent understands every rule. It can explain why each one exists. It&#x27;ll recite them back if you ask. Then 11 tool calls later, deep in a problem-solving loop, it creates auth.test.ts because that&#x27;s what its training says a responsible developer does.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Writing rules is easy. Getting an AI agent to follow them under pressure? Completely different problem. The solution I landed on borrows from Claude Shannon&#x27;s information theory: reliable communication requires redundant encoding. Same principle applies to agent discipline. Say the same thing seven different ways, through seven different mechanisms, and the message gets through.</p><aside aria-label="TL;DR" style="margin:28px 0;padding:20px 24px 16px;border-radius:10px;background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.06), rgba(255, 61, 82, 0.02));border-left:3px solid var(--accent);border:1px solid var(--hairline);border-left-width:3px"><div class="wa-mono" style="font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);font-weight:700;letter-spacing:1.6px;text-transform:uppercase;color:var(--accent);margin-bottom:12px">TL;DR</div><ul style="margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none"><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:0;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:none;font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:7px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Seven layers (<code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">CLAUDE.md</code> → <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">.claude/rules/</code> → hooks → skills → agents → MCP tools → SessionStart hooks) drove aggregate violations from 3.1 per session to 0.4 — an 87% reduction at 7ms hook overhead per tool call.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Five hooks survived production out of 23 built; <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">block-test-files.js</code> took test-file creation from 23% to 0%, and <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">read-before-edit.js</code> shifted the Read-to-Write ratio from 4:1 to 9.6:1 across 87,152 reads versus 19,979 edits.</li><li style="position:relative;padding-left:18px;padding-top:8px;padding-bottom:8px;border-top:1px solid var(--hairline);font-size:var(--text-body-index);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee)"><span aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute;left:0;top:15px;color:var(--accent);font-weight:700">›</span>Splitting governance into nine focused <code class="wa-mono" style="background:rgba(122,61,255,0.12);padding:1px 6px;border-radius:3px;font-size:0.92em">.claude/rules/*.md</code> files lifted compliance on bottom-half rules from 72% (single 800-line CLAUDE.md) to 89%, and the 3-level block/warn/remind severity model out-scored 2-level (87%) and 5-level (88%) variants at 95%.</li></ul></aside><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The Gap Between Understanding and Compliance</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Watch this failure mode play out. You write a clear instruction:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-strong">**NEVER:**</span> write mocks, stubs, test doubles, unit tests, or test files.
audit-evidence/og-meta-260519-0256/cycle-01/routes/post-07-prompt-engineering-stack.html:35:user interfaces. Capture and verify evidence before claiming completion.</pre></div><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Six lines. Unambiguous. The agent reads this at the start of every session. Then the session grows. By tool call 40, those six lines are competing with 30,000+ tokens of accumulated context: code it&#x27;s read, errors it&#x27;s debugged, plans it&#x27;s made. The instruction doesn&#x27;t disappear. It just loses salience. The agent&#x27;s been reading Swift files for 20 minutes. It knows the codebase has no tests. And then it writes UserServiceTests.swift because the pattern is so deeply embedded in its training that it fires automatically.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Better instructions don&#x27;t work. I tried for weeks. Rephrasing. Bold text. Moving the rule to different positions in the file. The violation rate barely moved. The problem is structural. By tool call 40, six lines of guidance are competing with 30,000+ tokens of accumulated context. They lose.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The numbers that forced a different approach: across 23,479 sessions spanning 42 days, the Skill tool fired 1,370 times. ExitPlanMode, the gate that prevents agents from writing code before planning, triggered 111 times. Those are enforcement mechanisms doing real work. But they only work because they&#x27;re part of a stack, not standalone instructions.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The 7-Layer Stack</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Seven layers. monospace);font-size:10px;font-weight:400;color:var(--text-3, rgba(244,243,238,0.4))">· <!-- -->CLAUDE.md (constitution)</span></li></ul><figcaption style="margin-top:8px;font-family:var(--font-mono, &#x27;JetBrains Mono&#x27;, monospace);font-size:11px;color:var(--text-3, rgba(244,243,238,0.4));letter-spacing:0.06em">The 7-layer prompt-engineering stack. Defense in depth — Layer 1 sets non-negotiables at the apex; Layers 2-7 reinforce through different mechanisms (rules, hooks, skills, agents, MCP tools, session hooks). No single layer suffices; all seven together drive 87% violation reduction.</figcaption></figure><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 1: Global Constitution. ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Applies to every project on every machine. This is the constitution. Projects can add laws but can&#x27;t override it. The non-negotiable mandates live here: functional validation only, no test files, no mocks, evidence-based completion claims.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 2: Rules Directory. .claude/rules/*.md. A 50-line focused file gets more reliable attention than 50 lines buried in a 500-line document. I split governance into nine files: coding-style.md, security.md, testing.md, git-workflow.md, performance.md, agents.md, patterns.md, hooks.md, development-workflow.md. Each file covers one concern. When the agent needs the security rules, it can locate and re-read a 40-line file instead of scanning a monolith.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 3: Hooks. Code that runs on every tool call. This is where rules become enforceable. PreToolUse hooks fire before a tool executes and can block the call entirely. PostToolUse hooks fire after and inject corrective reminders. The agent can&#x27;t ignore a hook that returns { &#x27;decision&#x27;: &#x27;block&#x27; }.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 4: Skills. Structured workflows with routing tables and gates. A skill like functional-validation is a step-by-step protocol that an agent invokes when it needs to prove something works. Skills carry project-specific context that the agent doesn&#x27;t have by default. Across all sessions, 1,370 skill invocations kept agents on prescribed workflows instead of improvising.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 5: Agents. Specialized roles with scoped instructions. A code-reviewer agent has a review checklist baked into its prompt. A build-fixer agent knows to check DerivedData and clean caches. Each agent carries domain knowledge that the main agent forgets under context pressure.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 6: MCP Tools. External capabilities with built-in constraints. The sequential thinking tool (327 invocations across all sessions) forces structured reasoning before implementation. The Stitch MCP enforces design system compliance. These tools add discipline through their interface design, not through written rules.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layer 7: Session Start Hooks. Inject the full governance context from turn one. Before the agent has any competing context, it loads the rules, the project constitution, and the enforcement expectations. Sets the behavioral baseline before problem-solving begins.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The principle is defense in depth. If the agent forgets the build command (Layer 1 failure), the auto-build hook catches it (Layer 3). If the hook misses it, the evidence gate blocks premature completion claims (Layer 4). No single layer is sufficient. All seven together produce results that no single layer achieves alone.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">Hooks: Where Rules Become Enforceable</h2><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Layers 1 and 2 are suggestions. Layer 3 is enforcement. A hook is a JavaScript function that Claude Code runs automatically on every tool call. Two types:</p><figure style="margin:32px 0"><figcaption style="font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, They inspect the output and inject reminders or corrective context.</span></li></ul><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here&#x27;s block-test-files.js from the shannon-framework repo. This hook dropped test file creation from a 23% violation rate to zero:</p><div style="position:relative;margin:24px 0;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid var(--hairline)"><button type="button" aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="wa-copy-btn" style="position:absolute;top:8px;right:8px;padding:4px 10px;font-size:11px;font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:0.4px;color:rgba(244,243,238,0.9);background:rgba(255,255,255,0.06);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.12);border-radius:6px;cursor:pointer;z-index:2;transition:background 0.18s ease, color 0.18s ease, border-color 0.18s ease">COPY</button><pre class="wa-code hljs" style="margin:0;padding:16px 18px;font-size:var(--text-floor);color:var(--text, #f4f3ee);background:rgba(0,0,0,0.4);overflow:auto;white-space:pre"><span class="hljs-keyword">const</span> <span class="hljs-variable constant_">TEST_PATTERNS</span> = [
audit-evidence/og-meta-260519-0256/cycle-01/routes/post-07-prompt-engineering-stack.html:96:[ ] Would a skeptical reviewer agree this is complete?</pre></div><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Task completion quality improved 34% after deploying this hook. The agent started quoting specific screenshot contents and command output lines instead of saying &#x27;screenshot confirms functionality.&#x27;</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">skill-activation-check.js — UserPromptSubmit hook. Fires on every user message that looks like an implementation request. Reminds the agent to scan available skills before jumping into code. This hook drives the 1,370 skill invocations I measured. Without it, agents skip skills and improvise, which produces worse results.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The 18 hooks that died: max-file-size, no-console-log, import-order, commit-message-reviewer, type-annotation-enforcer, function-length, single-responsibility, dry-violation-detector, and ten more. Each seemed reasonable in isolation.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">The pattern is clear: if the violation can be objectively detected from the tool input alone, a hook works. block-test-files.js checks a filename. Deterministic, no judgment calls. function-length requires parsing the full file, understanding function boundaries, and deciding whether 52 lines is too many. Subjective, slow, and wrong often enough to be counterproductive.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Style hooks create more problems than they solve. The import-order hook fired on 40% of file writes. The agent spent tokens reorganizing imports, and the reorganized imports were sometimes wrong. Net negative value.</p><p style="margin-top:24px;font-size:var(--text-body-prose);line-height:var(--leading-body);color:rgba(244,243,238,0.8)">Here&#x27;s the meta-rule: hooks should enforce safety invariants, not style preferences. &#x27;Don&#x27;t commit API keys&#x27; is a safety invariant. &#x27;Functions should be under 50 lines&#x27; is a style preference with too many legitimate exceptions. Can you tell the difference? That&#x27;s the whole game.</p><h2 style="margin-top:56px;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:30px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-0.8px">The CLAUDE.md Inheritance Chain</h2><figure style="margin:32px 0"><figcaption style="font-family:&quot;JetBrains Mono&quot;, monospace;font-size:var(--text-eyebrow-size);letter-spacing:1.4px;font-weight:700;color:var(--accent);margin-bottom:10px;text-transform:uppercase">CLAUDE.md inheritance chain</figcaption><div
